messages:
anya: Quick note — spotted an inconsistency between the API ref streaming example and the actual server behavior.
anya: The doc sample shows an SSE payload with plain JSON lines (Content-Type: text/event-stream, data: {...}), but server emits events with `event: delta` and the `data` object wraps tokens, e.g. `{type: 'token', token: '...'}`.
anya: This causes the JS/py SDK snippets to parse incorrectly.
anya: Repro steps:
anya: ```bash
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/chat/stream -d '{"messages": [{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```
anya: Current doc shows:
anya: ```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream

data: {"text":"hello"}

```
anya: Actual server emits:
anya: ```http
event: delta
data: {"type":"token","token":"hel"}

event: delta
data: {"type":"token","token":"lo"}

event: done
data: {"id":"...","meta":{}}
```
morgan: Ah thanks, that's why the SDK streaming iterator test failed for me.
morgan: Our JS snippet currently expects a single JSON per `data` and tries to JSON.parse to a message object. We need to update to handle `event` names and `type` inside data.
lee: I'll open a PR to align examples + SDK snippet. I'll also add an example showing how to parse both legacy and current formats.
lee: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/12901
sam: Can you include an OpenAPI example too? The OpenAPI sample currently uses `application/json` and not `text/event-stream`.
lee: Yep — added an OpenAPI request/response example in the PR. Snippet I added:
lee: ```yaml
paths:
  /v1/chat/stream:
    post:
      consumes:
        - text/event-stream
      responses:
        '200':
          content:
            text/event-stream:
              schema:
                type: string
              examples:
                sse: |
                  event: delta\n
                  data: {"type":"token","token":"hi"}\n
```
morgan: Also pushed updated SDK example for python async iterate:
morgan: ```py
async for event in client.chat.stream(...):
    # event is {"event":"delta","data":{"type":"token","token":"..."}}
    if event['event'] == 'delta' and event['data']['type'] == 'token':
        print(event['data']['token'], end='')
    elif event['event'] == 'done':
        break
```
